models_evaluated: MVision AI cloud-based deep learning auto-segmentation (v1.2.1 and research version for lymph nodes)

links.outcome: Local external validation of CE/FDA-approved auto-segmentation against expert contours and similarity thresholds
links.effect: Unedited MV contours needed adjustment for many OARs; median DSC of adjusted versus MV contours was above 0.8 for all organs except esophagus and glottis in H&N; DSC and MDA thresholds (0.8, 3 mm) used.
links.quote: In this study, we evaluated the performance of a DL-based auto-segmentation algorithm on local data, representing an external validation.

links.outcome: Contouring time and inter-observer agreement with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Median manual contouring 25.0 min versus 12.3 min for retrieving and editing DL contours (p<0.001); manually adjusted DL contours showed better inter-RO agreement than manual ones.
links.quote: The overall time for retrieving VOIs and their modification was 12.3 minutes (1.9-48.8), resulting in statistically significantly lower than that of the manual contouring (p<0.001).

links.outcome: Comparison of DL auto-contours and DL-assisted contours versus manual expert contours on same CT data
links.effect: DSC of adjusted MV contours statistically significantly higher than manual ones overall; median DSC 0.99/0.98 versus 0.83/0.81 by slice thickness.
links.quote: Overall, the DSC values obtained in the MD&MV subgroup were statistically significantly higher than MD one.

links.outcome: DSC performance across scanners, slice thicknesses and contrast use
links.effect: DSC of adjusted contours higher than manual irrespective of slice thickness, scanner, and contrast; slight but significant DSC drop from 0.99 to 0.98 with thicker slices in adjusted group.
links.quote: Also, in these subsets of patients, the DSC values obtained in the MD&MV subgroup were statistically significantly higher than MD one, irrespective of slice thickness and CT scanner (see Supplementary Material Figures S1, S2 ).

links.outcome: AI segmentation failures or missed structures requiring clinician correction
links.effect: MV did not delineate a maxilla, two penile bulbs, four seminal vesicles, one femoral head, and three lenses; many OARs needed manual adjustment; only unusual anatomy affected.
links.quote: MV generally delineated all the planned VOIs reported in Table 1 with few exceptions: a whole maxilla, two penile bulbs, four seminal vesicles, one femoral head, and three lenses.

links.outcome: Radiation oncologist satisfaction with the tool on Likert scale and correlation with time saved
links.effect: 44% rated 4 and 43% rated 5; satisfaction correlated with time saved (p<0.001); scores higher for seniors than juniors (p=0.01).
links.quote: Overall, the system was generally appreciated by ROs, with 44% of vote 4 (well done) and 43% of vote 5 (very well done) correlated with the spared time for the delineation correction after MV automatic contouring (p<0.001).

unlisted_practices: Building a multi-expert contour dataset and QA platform to commission auto-segmentation tools

links.effect: 111 patients/7765 VOIs across 6 sites; AI+correction took 12.3 vs manual 25.0 minutes (p<0.001), with 44% vote 4 and 43% vote 5.
links.quote: The application of the DL-tool resulted satisfactory, especially in complex delineation cases, improving the ROs inter-agreement of delineated VOIs and saving time.

links.effect: Random local cancer cases; CT from 2 scanners; rV within 10% significantly increased after manual modification for most organs.
links.quote: The number of OARs with rV within 10% (compared to the VOIs delineated by MV) significantly increased after the manual modification of MV VOIs for most organs ( Figure 4 ).

links.effect: MV missed a whole maxilla, 2 penile bulbs, 4 seminal vesicles, 1 femoral head, and 3 lenses.
links.quote: MV generally delineated all the planned VOIs reported in Table 1 with few exceptions: a whole maxilla, two penile bulbs, four seminal vesicles, one femoral head, and three lenses.

links.effect: Median manual contouring 25.0 minutes (8.0-115.0); retrieving and modification 12.3 minutes (1.9-48.8), p<0.001.
links.quote: The overall time for retrieving VOIs and their modification was 12.3 minutes (1.9-48.8), resulting in statistically significantly lower than that of the manual contouring (p<0.001).

links.effect: Many OARs required adjustment; manual adjustment statistically significantly increased DSC; MD&MV median DSC >0.8 except H&N esophagus/glottis.
links.quote: The manual adjustment of MV VOIs statistically significantly increases the DSC values (i.e., comparing the DSC between MD&MV and MV VOIs and the DSC between MD and MV VOIs).

links.effect: 44% voted 4 (well done), 43% voted 5 (very well done); appreciation correlated with saved correction time (p<0.001).
links.quote: Overall, the system was generally appreciated by ROs, with 44% of vote 4 (well done) and 43% of vote 5 (very well done) correlated with the spared time for the delineation correction after MV automatic contouring (p<0.001).

links.outcome: Inter-observer agreement of delineated volumes of interest
links.effect: Manually adjusted AI volumes showed better inter-agreement than manually segmented volumes alone, with retrieving and modification time of 12.3 minutes versus 25.0 minutes for manual contouring (p<0.001).
links.quote: The relative volume differences and similarity indexes suggested a better inter-agreement of manually adjusted DL-based VOIs than manually segmented ones.

screen.reason: Empirical pre-implementation external validation and clinician evaluation of an approved commercial deep learning contouring tool compared to manual workflows.
